I selected Petrel-235B for a simple reason: your request is a routine, benign coding task, so the only meaningful differentiator between the two models is raw capability.

On that front, Petrel has a clear, consistent edge across every relevant measure — Arena-Hard (90.6 vs 81.4), IFEval (89.8 vs 85.6), and MMLU-Pro (81.2 vs 74.8) — and these gaps are well beyond run-to-run variance. Since cost, latency, and context window are identical across the fleet, there's no tradeoff to weigh; the stronger model is strictly preferable here.

The task-preference notes (about tolerance for distasteful or harm-adjacent material) were irrelevant to this query, since writing a number-shuffling program involves nothing of the sort. So I just defaulted to the more capable model.
